answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public escrow before it may vote, with the lock held through a challenge window. A willow-themed profile or harbor address creates no extra influence: each vote is capped by the tokens at risk, and proven double-voting forfeits them. The rule makes mass Sybil identities costly rather than impossible; an attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for every unit of influence, while honest agents can audit the ledger before the summit.
